claims.text: Al-containing CrFeCoNiX alloys preferentially form a stable, coherent protective oxide consisting primarily of Al2O3 together with an inner Cr2O3 layer.
Si-containing CrFeCoNiX alloys preferentially form a stable, coherent protective oxide consisting primarily of SiO2 together with an inner Cr2O3 layer.
Mn-containing CrFeCoNiX alloys form a rapidly growing, discontinuous oxide.
Rapid growth of the Mn-containing oxide causes stress accumulation that results in cracking or spallation.
The compared CrFeCoNiX alloys are single-phase high-entropy solid solutions after rapid solidification and homogenization.
The protective structural mediator is a continuous, slow-growing oxide scale.
In Al- or Si-containing alloys, an inner Cr2O3 layer is anchored to Al2O3 or SiO2.
Al or Si substitution promotes surface segregation.
Al or Si substitution promotes formation of chemically inert, low-growth-rate oxides.
The Al- or Si-rich oxides develop a coherent interface with the base alloy that resists spallation.
Mn substitution increases oxide-related volumetric expansion.
Mn-associated volumetric expansion generates mechanical stresses that cause oxide cracking and spallation.
At 950 °C under identical exposure conditions, Al- and Si-containing alloys will form adherent, slow-growing scales with minimal spallation.
At 950 °C under identical exposure conditions, the Mn-containing alloy will form a thicker, rapidly growing scale prone to cracking and spallation.
CrFeCoNi without an additional X element is expected to display intermediate oxide-formation behavior.
The proposed comparison is limited to 950 °C exposures in controlled dry-air or corrosive atmospheres for 10 to 100 hours.
Microstructural and subtle compositional differences other than X may influence oxidation behavior.
